claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I have one child I'm asking about - Alex. He's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 13 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are specific circumstances where you may still be eligible for Child Benefit.

**Which country are you currently living in, and are you or your partner a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad, but I'm not a Crown servant - I don't work for the diplomatic service or the armed forces or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since you're living abroad and not a Crown servant, I need to understand your situation better.

**Which specific country are you currently living in? This is important because Child Benefit eligibility while abroad depends on whether you're living in certain countries (such as EEA countries or countries with specific agreements with the UK).**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into the specific country right now. Does it really matter which one? I just need to know if I can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your concern, but yes, unfortunately the specific country does matter quite a bit for Child Benefit eligibility when living abroad.

According to the rules, you can only get Child Benefit while living abroad in very specific circumstances:
- If you're in certain countries (such as EEA countries or countries with specific social security agreements with the UK), or
- If you're a Crown servant (which you've indicated you're not)

Without knowing which country you're in, I cannot determine whether you fall into one of the eligible categories for claiming Child Benefit from abroad.

**Is there a reason you're hesitant to share which country you're in? Or alternatively, are you planning to move back to the UK in the near future?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. Well, I'm not in an EEA country, and I'm not planning to move back to the UK anytime soon. I just wanted to see if there was any way I could still claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that important information.

Based on what you've told me:
- You're living abroad in a country that is not an EEA country
- You're not a Crown servant (diplomat, armed forces, etc.)
- You're not planning to move back to the UK soon

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can only claim Child Benefit while living abroad if you're living in certain specific countries or if you're a Crown servant. Since neither of these applies to your situation, unfortunately you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex while you remain living abroad outside the UK and outside those specific qualifying countries.

If your circumstances were to change - for example, if you moved back to the UK or moved to an EEA country - then you could potentially claim Child Benefit at that time, assuming you meet the other eligibility criteria.

Let me provide my assessment:
